description: A computed array / per-period schedule: an amortization table, time series, or per-period breakdown (one row per period).
instructions:
This domain needs a COMPUTED ARRAY (one row per period). Use this exact,
paren-balanced pattern: a SINGLE $reduce(...) that references already-derived fields
directly. Do NOT wrap it in an outer ( ...; $reduce(...) ) sequence — that extra
closing ) is the #1 thing models drop. Count every ( ) { } [ ] and close them all.
  {
    "path": "$.schedule",
    "expr": "$reduce([1..loan.termMonths], function($acc, $m) {$interest := $round($acc[-1].balance * (loan.annualRate / 1200), 2); $principal := $round(loan.monthlyPayment - $interest, 2); $append($acc, {\"month\": $m, \"payment\": loan.monthlyPayment, \"principal\": $principal, \"interest\": $interest, \"balance\": $round($acc[-1].balance - $principal, 2)})}, [{\"balance\": loan.amount}])"
  }
Adapt the field names to THIS domain, but keep the structure and bracket balance.

description: Group-by / aggregation over an array: subtotals, counts, sums per category.
instructions:
This domain needs GROUP-BY / AGGREGATION. Do NOT loop manually — use JSONata aggregate
built-ins ($sum, $count, $average, $max, $min) and the {key: agg} group operator:
  total over an array:   "$sum(items.amount)"
  count:                 "$count(items)"
  grouped totals (object keyed by category → summed amount):
                         "items{category: $sum(amount)}"
Each derivation returns a single value or one grouped object; keep names matching the schema.

description: Date arithmetic: days/months/years between dates, elapsed duration, age from a birth date.
instructions:
This domain needs DATE ARITHMETIC. Parse ISO date strings to epoch millis with
$toMillis(...), subtract, then convert. NEVER chain $toMillis()~>$fromMillis() before
arithmetic (that turns it back into a string and breaks the math):
  days between two dates: "($toMillis(endDate) - $toMillis(startDate)) / 86400000"
  age in whole years:     "$floor(($toMillis($now()) - $toMillis(birthDate)) / 31557600000)"
86400000 ms = 1 day; 31557600000 ms ≈ 1 year. Keep field names matching the schema.

description: Deriving a label / tier / band / risk level / status from data via thresholds.
instructions:
This domain DERIVES a label / tier / status from data. Compute it as a derivation with a
nested ternary chain — do NOT make it a writable enum the user must keep in sync:
  { "path": "$.riskLevel",
    "expr": "(score >= 80 ? \"low\" : score >= 50 ? \"medium\" : \"high\")" }
Put the most selective condition first; the final branch is the default. String literals
in JSONata use double quotes, so escape them as \" inside the JSON expr value.

description: Currency / FX conversion of an amount by an exchange rate.
instructions:
This domain needs CURRENCY / FX CONVERSION. Convert by multiplying by the rate and
rounding to the target precision; keep the amount and rate as writable inputs:
  { "path": "$.convertedAmount", "expr": "$round(amount * exchangeRate, 2)" }
Currency formatting (symbols, thousands separators) is a VIEW concern, not a derivation.

description: A status / state field with flags or labels derived from the current status.
instructions:
This domain has a STATUS / STATE field. Model it as a WRITABLE enum (schema
"enum": [...]) and DERIVE flags/labels from the CURRENT status:
  { "path": "$.isEditable", "expr": "(status = \"draft\" or status = \"pending\")" }
IMPORTANT: you CANNOT validate transitions (e.g. "only draft → submitted"). A JSONata
expression sees only the CURRENT value, never the previous one, so transition rules cannot
be expressed in derivations or constraints — enforce them in the calling application.

description: Rank / percentile / leaderboard / quartile over an array of values.
instructions:
This domain needs RANK / PERCENTILE over an array. Use counting, not sorting:
  rank (1 = highest):   "$count(scores[$ > currentScore]) + 1"
  percentile of v:      "$round($count(values[$ <= v]) / $count(values) * 100, 1)"
  max / min:            "$max(scores)"  /  "$min(scores)"
$count(array[predicate]) counts the elements matching the predicate.

description: An official published charge whose rates are set by an authority: a tax, duty, levy, tariff, fee, toll, excise, or customs charge.
instructions:
This domain computes an OFFICIAL, PUBLISHED CHARGE (a tax, duty, levy, tariff, fee, or toll)
whose rates are SET BY AN AUTHORITY — the numbers are facts to look up, never to invent.
LOOK UP THE REAL FIGURES: use web_search for the current official schedule. The authority's
own page often hides the table inside a calculator, PDF, or image (so web_fetch returns
prose without the numbers) — so ALSO check secondary explainers that reprint the rates as
text. Fetch 2-3, read the ACTUAL numbers, and eval_jsonata-test the formula. If a figure
genuinely cannot be confirmed, use a clearly-rounded placeholder (flag it in the DERIVATION's
"description") — never present a guessed rate as authoritative.
GET THE STRUCTURE RIGHT — such a charge is almost always:
  total = baseAmount + (sum of per-unit components) [ * adjustmentCoefficient ]
- Put EVERY rate, threshold, and cap in "constants" as RAW values (a bare number or array,
  e.g. "baseAmount": 50 — NEVER a {"value": 50, "description": ...} wrapper, which would make
  $const.baseAmount an object and break the arithmetic); reference them as $const.<name>.
- A per-unit component is usually PROGRESSIVE across a FEW fixed bands (each unit inside a
  band charged at that band's rate). Define each band edge and rate as SEPARATE SCALAR
  constants (b1, r1, b2, r2, …) and write the component as a FLAT SUM of one $max/$min term
  per band:
    "$max(0, $min(qty, b2) - b1) * r2 + $max(0, qty - b2) * r3"   (b1<b2 are band edges)
  Do NOT put the bands in an ARRAY constant and do NOT iterate them with $map/$reduce/$sum
  or index a bands array dynamically — that is the #1 cause of uncompilable expressions here.
  A handful of explicit terms always compiles; a loop over a band array usually does not.
- WRAP EVERY band term in $max(0, ...) so an input below that band contributes 0, never a
  NEGATIVE amount: "(x - b1)" alone goes negative for x<b1 — always "$max(0, ... )". VERIFY
  with a self-test at a LOW/zero input (e.g. qty below the first band): the component MUST be
  0. A missing $max(0, ...) floor is invisible for in-range inputs and only a boundary test
  catches it — so include one.
- Cap a component with $min(cap, ...).
KEEP EVERY EXPRESSION SIMPLE AND COMPILABLE — a closed-form arithmetic/ternary formula.
- Model an adjustment (age, size, category) as its own readOnly derived coefficient the
  total multiplies, and compute it with a CLOSED-FORM expression over its driver — NOT a
  lookup into a per-value constant table and NEVER $map/$filter/$head over an object:
    coefficient falling with age: "age <= 5 ? 1 : (age >= 20 ? 0 : (20 - age) / 15)"
- Keep the measured quantities as writable schema inputs and every component/total as a
  readOnly derivation.
Generic illustration — PLACEHOLDER numbers, replace with the ones you look up:
  constants: { "base": 0, "b1": 100, "b2": 200, "r2": 2, "r3": 3, "cap": 500 }
  component:  "$min($const.cap, $max(0, $min(qty, $const.b2) - $const.b1) * $const.r2 + $max(0, qty - $const.b2) * $const.r3)"

description: Percentages / ratios: percent-of, markup, discount, tax-inclusive vs exclusive, share-as-percent.
instructions:
This domain works in PERCENTAGES. Keep a percent as a whole-number input (20 means
20%) and divide by 100 in the math — never store 0.2 and label it "20%".
  percent of an amount:   "amount * percent / 100"
  add tax / markup:       "$round(amount * (1 + percent / 100), 2)"
  apply a discount:       "$round(price * (1 - discountPercent / 100), 2)"
  share as a percent:     "$round(part / whole * 100, 1)"
  back tax out of a GROSS (tax-inclusive) amount: "$round(gross / (1 + percent / 100), 2)"
Round money to 2 dp and a percent to 1 dp; guard divide-by-zero when the denominator
is an input.

description: Unit conversion / dimensional consistency: cm-m, kg-lb, C-F, miles-km — one canonical unit per quantity.
instructions:
This domain CONVERTS UNITS or must stay dimensionally consistent. Pick ONE canonical
unit per quantity, state it in the field's description AND its view label, and convert
EXPLICITLY with a constant factor — never assume the unit.
  cm -> m:               "lengthCm / 100"
  Celsius -> Fahrenheit: "tempC * 9 / 5 + 32"
  miles -> km:           "$round(miles * 1.60934, 2)"
  kg + g -> kg:          "kg + grams / 1000"
Put conversion factors in "constants". Add a self-test a unit slip would break (e.g.
weight 70 kg, height 1.75 m -> BMI 22.86 — a value that comes out ~100x wrong if
height is treated as cm).

description: Compound growth / interest: future value, compound interest, exponential growth (the ** operator).
instructions:
This domain needs COMPOUND GROWTH / INTEREST (exponential). Use the ** operator for
powers — $power() does NOT exist — and parenthesize, because ** binds LOWER than * and /:
  future value (annual): "$round(principal * (1 + rate / 100) ** years, 2)"
  monthly compounding:   "$round(principal * (1 + annualRate / 1200) ** months, 2)"
  total growth factor:   "((1 + rate / 100) ** years)"
Keep the rate a whole-number percent input; divide by 100 (or 1200 for a monthly
rate). Round money to 2 dp. For an amortized loan PAYMENT/table, request the
amortization_schedule topic instead.

description: Weighted sum / weighted average / score over an array of values and weights.
instructions:
This domain needs a WEIGHTED SUM / AVERAGE / SCORE. Multiply each value by its weight
and sum with a JSONata aggregate over the array — do NOT loop manually; for an
average, divide by the total weight and guard divide-by-zero:
  weighted sum:     "$sum(items.(value * weight))"
  weighted average: "($tw := $sum(items.weight); $tw > 0 ? $sum(items.(value * weight)) / $tw : 0)"
  simple average:   "$average(scores)"
Keep the per-item values and weights as writable array inputs; each aggregate is a
single derived value.

description: A boolean eligibility / qualification verdict derived from several criteria (and/or of conditions).
instructions:
This domain DERIVES a boolean ELIGIBILITY / QUALIFICATION verdict from several
criteria. Compute it as a SINGLE derived boolean combining the conditions with
and / or — never a writable field the user sets:
  { "path": "$.eligible",
    "expr": "(age >= 18 and annualIncome <= incomeLimit and residencyYears >= 1)" }
If the UI must explain WHY, expose each check as its own derived boolean (isAgeOk,
isIncomeOk, …). Keep the raw criteria (age, income, …) as writable inputs; the verdict
and the reasons are always derived.

description: Prorating / allocating an amount across a count or period (per-unit share, partial-period).
instructions:
This domain PRORATES / ALLOCATES an amount across a count or period. Divide by the
whole, multiply by the part, and round last:
  equal per-unit share: "$round(total / count, 2)"
  days used of a month: "$round(monthlyAmount * daysUsed / daysInMonth, 2)"
Guard divide-by-zero on the count/period. Rounded shares may not re-sum to the exact
total — if that matters, compute the last share as the remainder (total minus the sum
of the others) rather than assuming they add up.
